hypotheses.claim: Second-line activity is driven by lineage-specific target dependence: compounds with targets expressed or essential in a given tissue will show activity there, while compounds without such targets will not.
predictions: AXL inhibitor R-428 active in AXL-high lines (e.g., A375, PC3) and inactive in AXL-low lines
ATR inhibitor VE-821 active in lines with high replication stress (e.g., HT29, MCF7)
otilonium/sulbutiamine (CACNA1C/unknown) show broad or non-lineage-specific activity

hypotheses.claim: Second-line activity is dominated by shared systematic response and vehicle-norm threshold effects, so line choice has limited biological specificity and many compounds will show similar activity patterns across lines.
predictions: Activity labels correlate more with compound identity than with tissue lineage
Compounds with no annotated target (sulbutiamine, tirasemtiv) show activity patterns comparable to targeted compounds
Different second lines for the same compound often yield concordant activity labels

evidence_gaps: No measured target expression or dependency data for these lines
No dose-response or vehicle-threshold details per line
No replicate or batch information to separate systematic response from lineage effect
Repurposing Hub/MAP annotations are not causal and may be incomplete
Activity is a vehicle-norm threshold, not viability

object.revised_memory: A375 first-line: only R-428 (AXL) active; all others inactive. Candidate probabilities are low across lines, with YAPC generally lowest. H1 (lineage-specific target dependence) weakened because most targeted compounds inactive in A375; H2 (shared systematic/vehicle-threshold response) better fits. Chose YAPC for most to test low-activity baseline; HT29 for VE-821. Activity remains vehicle-norm threshold, not viability.
